newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland bank gov sees inflation risks clearly up.
newsitem.headline: Finland bank gov sees inflation risks clearly up.

text.p: Bank of Finland governor Sirkka Hamalainen said on Monday that inflation risks had increased clearly.
"Inflation risks have increased clearly," Hamalainen told a news conference on the publication of the 2/1997 issue of the central bank's Markka & Talous (Markka and the Economy) publication.
"Asset values have been rising strongly," she said, referring to shares, raw wood prices and housing prices.
"In this context it is good to remember the wisdom ... that what goes up must come down," Hamalainen said.

Rising asset values as such would not jeopardise the central bank's core inflation target of two percent, "but they reflect future price expectations and when asset values rise, people and banks feel they are somehow more wealthy ... which may boost demand," Hamalainen said.
"This is a problem only to extent that it is reflected in real inflation," she said.
She said the economy was in such a situation that higher demand even from tax relief -- as called for by some unions to compensate for moderate pay hikes -- could be dangerous.
On share prices, she said they had been low in relation to profitability and real values "but changes as large as this are problematic," she said.
On the Helsinki bourse, the HEX all-share index has risen 26 percent this year and 84 percent since the end of 1995.
The governor said some estimates suggested the economy was nearing a situation where all production capacity is used, and that some sectors experience bottlenecks.
She mentioned the electrotechnical industry, the information technology sector and parts of the financial sector as suffering from a lack of skilled labour. @
"In such a situation, companies' margins easily start rising, wages start rising and, if wage-wage linkages are still in force, the situation easily gets harder," she said.

"A key issue as far as the inflation outlook is concerned is whether and how moderate pay deals are made," she said, adding that the bank's forecast of 1998 core inflation rising slightly above two percent was based on the assumption of moderate hikes.
Traditionally, rising wages have been preceded by higher asset and raw wood prices, and "we can only hope this link has been broken," she said. @
The central bank said in a statement that inflation risks had increased but that the current outlook did not portend a change in the stance of monetary policy.
"An increase in the probability that inflation will exceed the forecast rate would force the central to consider monetary tightening," the bank said.
